body:
The material in front of me is the account and the rival; the objection slot is empty, so the rival's criticisms are the only criticism in play, and I won't invent another. The two nodes agree on more than they contest — the diagnosis is underdetermined, there are at least three live readings (later reconstruction failure, scope divergence at the moment of agreement, and the arguments doing some other work entirely), the avoidance is a symptom to understand rather than a defect to correct, and no adjudication of past agreements will settle anything because memory is exactly what is contested. All of that I keep. The live disagreement is sequence: what the first move should be, and what each possible outcome of it would mean. Four decisions follow.

First, I take up the rival's probe as the opening move, but I revise the weakness attached to it. The rival said the probe cannot reach what was actually agreed because recollection is already contested. True, but misaimed: the probe's target is the structure of the divergence, not the facts of the past. If one flatmate reports 'every week' and the other 'just that once,' the locus of the disagreement is recurrence regardless of whose memory is right. Read that way, the probe is stronger than the rival credited. The weakness the rival missed: recounting a disputed agreement can re-open it, and the asker is one of the three flatmates — a party to some of these disputes, with an unreliable memory of their own — now cast as broker between the other two. Cheap mitigations exist: the asker answers the question about themselves first, aloud, including where they may have been wrong; the question is identical for both flatmates; nobody relays an answer verbatim.

Second, I unbundle the account's package. The written record survives conditionally, matched to what the probe returns: if disagreements cluster on recurrence, a record with an explicit recurrence field is the narrow fix; if they cluster on scope, the fix may be cheaper than any record — a spoken read-back at the moment of agreement ('so that is dishes Monday and Thursday, this week, then we re-agree'), which works even if nothing is ever written; if on timing, deadline conventions. The weekly check-in stays in reserve, for two reasons: each new ritual is a cost in a household where one member is already withdrawing from conversations, and deploying everything at once would confound the reading of each move. The probe exists to say which fix fits; spending that information by applying all the remedies first would waste it.

Third, I revise the account's falsification test using the rival's relocation point, and in doing so answer the question the rival left open. Persistence of arguments after writing is not clean evidence, since a badly scoped record is consistent with every reading. The better observable is where disputes attach once a record exists: if they attach to the record's terms ('did bins mean every week?'), the scope reading gains weight; if they attach to the record itself ('why is my name on this and yours not?'), the standing-negotiation reading gains. Relocation is therefore informationally an improvement even when it is not a harmonious one — the argument's new location is data — but only if someone is watching for it with the rule stated in advance; otherwise it is just a new argument.

Fourth, on the avoiding friend, the rival's reframing absorbs the account's proposal almost entirely. The account wanted one private conversation to learn what makes the group conversations costly; the rival warned that making withdrawal the subject may reproduce the dynamic that produced it. The probe gives the account what it wanted at lower risk: the friend is asked the same content question as everyone, their behaviour is not the topic, and whether they engage is itself evidence about what they were avoiding. I therefore set aside the standalone private approach as a separate move, with one trigger condition neither node stated: if the friend declines even a symmetric content question asked of everyone, the avoidance can no longer be read as a response to the group format, and a direct conversation about the conversations (in the rival's framing, 'I want to hear your view of them') or outside help comes onto the table. Until then, their avoidance is not raised with them at all.

What I leave open is most of the substance: which reading holds, whether the load is in fact uneven, whether the disagreements concentrate on one person, whether the friend engages, whether a record would calm or inflame. One limit shared by both nodes deserves stating: every proposed move runs through one of the three flatmates, a party rather than an observer, and each move is an intervention the other two will hear as such. There is no neutral first step available — only steps whose costs are named in advance and whose outcomes are read by rules fixed before the outcomes are known.

So what I currently propose to take up is a sequence, not a verdict: probe first, with the questions and the reading rules fixed in advance; let the cluster pattern select the narrowest fix; keep the record conditional and the check-in deferred; treat any relocation of the argument as data; and let the friend's response to a symmetric question decide whether the avoidance itself needs to become the subject. Every part of that is revisable the moment the household answers back.
commitments:
Taking this up means adopting an ordering, a set of constraints, and four explicit decision rules — each detachable from the rest.

The central commitment is ordering probe before remedy. That is a proposed application, not a finding. Its ground is that the probe's answers discriminate among readings the material cannot decide between; its named cost is that asking can re-ignite disputes and casts the asker as broker. Whoever takes it up commits to the mitigations (the asker answers the question about themselves first and aloud, identical wording to both flatmates, no verbatim relaying of answers) and to letting the probe's own failure count against the ordering: if asking re-ignites an argument or the friend withdraws further, that is evidence this sequence was wrong for this household, not resistance to be explained away.

Second, a claim I flag as mine: the probe measures where reports diverge, not whose memory is true, and on that ground it is stronger than the rival's stated weakness allowed. The commitment that comes with it is restrictive — the probe must never be used to adjudicate a past agreement, since that use turns it back into the memory contest both nodes warned against. A reader who rejects my 'structure not truth' reading should drop the probe entirely, because under their reading it has no discriminating power.

Third, the remedies stay conditional and deferred: record-with-recurrence-field, spoken read-back, or deadline conventions, selected by cluster type, and the weekly check-in withheld unless agreements keep being made and disputed after the narrow fix. I commit to no remedy in advance. The dependence to note: this apparatus is void if the answers do not cluster — in that case the commitment is to bring the standing-negotiation and load-distribution questions forward rather than to fit a remedy anyway.

Fourth, the revised observable — where disputes attach once a record exists — is offered as more informative than the account's persist-or-not test, and as the resolution of the rival's open question about whether relocation improves or delays. Taking it up commits one to writing down, before any record exists, what each attachment-site would count for, and to holding to that rule afterward. Without the pre-stated rule the observation degrades into post hoc fitting, and I would not defend it in that form.

Fifth, the trigger condition on the friend — non-engagement with a symmetric content question is what moves the avoidance from something to observe to something to raise directly — is a proposed decision rule and the shakiest item here, since silence has many mundane causes. It inherits every uncertainty in both nodes' readings of the avoidance; treating it as one weak signal rather than a verdict is part of the commitment.

Unresolved and carried forward: the diagnosis itself; the load-distribution question, which my sequence cannot reach directly any more than either node could; the asker's position as interested party, mitigated but not removable; and the chance that none of these routes is right — a mediator, a different division of labour, or simply living with looser agreements may serve better, and nothing in the material ranks them. A cheap failure mode sits at step one: if the user cannot ask the question without it being heard as taking sides, everything downstream is void, and noticing that early would itself be a result.

What I actually propose to take up from here: run the probe under the pre-stated rules, report what each flatmate says the disagreement was about, and re-examine which reading the answers support before any remedy is installed. That is a commitment to the next observation, not to the truth of the synthesis.
